name: Tabrimmon
title: Father of Ben-Hadad, an Aramean king
summary: Tabrimmon was the son of Hezion and father of Ben-Hadad I, king of Aram (Syria) with its capital in Damascus. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in connection with King Asa's attempt to form an alliance with Ben-Hadad against Baasha, king of Israel. His significance lies mainly in his role as a link in the Aramean royal line of Damascus.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Aramean royal line
keyEvents.description: Tabrimmon is mentioned as the son of Hezion and father of Ben-Hadad, king of Aram who resided in Damascus. This places him within the Aramean dynasty.

keyEvents.title: King Asa's alliance with Ben-Hadad
keyEvents.description: King Asa of Judah sent silver and gold to Tabrimmon's son Ben-Hadad to break his covenant with Baasha, king of Israel, and instead form an alliance with Judah.

keyEvents.title: Ben-Hadad's attack on Israel
keyEvents.description: As a result of the alliance with Asa, Tabrimmon's son Ben-Hadad sent his commanders against the cities of Israel and captured Ijon, Dan, Abel-Beth-Maacah, and all Kinneret with the land of Naphtali.

keyEvents.title: The Parallel Account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The same event where Asa seeks help from Ben-Hadad, son of Tabrimmon, is also described in 2 Chronicles, where Asa is rebuked by the seer Hanani for trusting in the king of Aram instead of the Lord.
